Subject: Post-call recap: Solstice Health dedicated capacity qualification & next steps

Hi Aisha / Marcus —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I’ve pulled the recommended capacity/ops options into two tracks (proof-of-concept vs. committed) to make procurement conversations easier.

1) What we heard (pain + goals)
- Primary pain: inconsistent latency and noisy multi-tenant interference during peak inference windows (batch billing spikes have impacted cost predictability).
- Goal: Serve triaged patient-facing summarization + clinical search with predictable p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
- Compliance: PHI-in-scope; must be either single-tenant dedicated pools or Private deployment with documented KMS integration.

2) Qualification summary (what we recommend now)
- Short-term (Proof-of-concept): 2-node reserved pool (NVMe-backed A10/A30 equivalent), single-tenant reservation to validate isolation and latency. Target throughput: ~60k tokens/min sustained; p95 gen latency target <= 200ms for short chat requests.
- Committed path: 8-GPU reserved pool (dedicated), isolation lane for Solstice, built-in burst policy to escalate into additional capacity for scheduled load (up to +40% for short windows). SLA guardrail: 99.9% uptime, SLOs measured per-route; we’ll instrument token-level cost/latency dashboards.
- Security: KMS envelope encryption, customer-managed keys available in Private or Dedicated with VPC peering. Audit logs and model access logs retained as agreed.

3) Risk & open questions
- Procurement timeline and PO cadence (we discussed a 60–90 day procurement window).
- Approval required from InfoSec on key management doc (we’ll supply the KMS integration checklist).
- Burst credit terms (how long can they sustain burst without additional commit).

4) Proposed next steps & owners
- Send draft SOW + isolation diagram (attached) — Owner: Priya (I’ve attached a starter draft). Timeline: by EOD 6/10.
- Technical deep-dive (architecture + performance): schedule 60–75 minute session with Jordan and Ben — action: Marcus to propose 2 slots (target next week).
- Procurement options: Ben to outline 60-day trial vs. immediate commit economics and a sample license/PO language.

If this matches your understanding, say so and we’ll get the SOW updated for procurement. If not, I’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Priya Natarajan

Quick internal note (Ben) — copying on next steps from an ops/finance perspective: 

- Burst policy options: we can do two flavors 
  * Auto-burst (pre-approved buffer included in commit) — typical for Dedicated customers; consumes committed units but can be capped daily.
  * Credit-based burst (expires after 30 days) — safer for finance, lets them control spend.
- Recommendation: offer the credit-based burst in the SOW as default, with an option to convert to auto-burst once procurement completes. Keeps Solstice comfortable.
- Pricing estimate: ballpark for 8-GPU reserved pool with enterprise support + 1yr commit: $XX,XXX–$YY,YYY/month depending on model family and quantization profile. I’ll prepare ranges and a short appendix.

Action: Priya will attach the initial SOW; Jordan can host the technical deep-dive and bring the ops runbook.
